description: Generated from phase package manifests, detected audio assets, and benchmark-authored audio provenance.

audio.strategy: Live synthesis only. The single Phase 1 piano voice is generated in the browser with Web Audio oscillators (six inharmonic sine partials, per-partial exponential decay, velocity-dependent partial levels and low-pass cutoff). No recorded or bundled audio files are used.

generatedSources.name: Phase 1 additive piano voice
generatedSources.description: Six sine partials per note at equal-tempered frequencies with a small inharmonic stretch (B = 0.0004), amplitudes proportional to k^-1.1 and rising with velocity, a velocity-scaled low-pass (1.2–10.2 kHz), exponential decay with a note-length-dependent time constant, and a release ramp on note-off. Generated at note-on; not a recording.
generatedSources.stealing: released tails first, then sustained voices, then held voices; oldest first within each class

notes: No sample sets are bundled in Phase 1. Grand, Upright and Electric recorded sample sets are Phase 2 scope; the piano spec allows honest synthesis for Phase 1.
No generated buffer is described as a recording. Nothing in the bundle is recorded audio.
The Web Audio path is: each voice -> voice low-pass -> master gain (0.3) -> AudioContext destination. No bypass.

The AudioContext is created on the first user gesture. If Web Audio is missing the instrument reports a labelled silent fallback; if the context refuses to resume it reports an error. The status line in the page shows which applies.
Pointer and computer-keyboard velocity is fixed at 100 in Phase 1 (KB Touch is Phase 2). MIDI uses the incoming note velocity.
Sustain applies to every voice in Phase 1 because there are no layers yet. Per-layer SUSTPED routing is Phase 2.

Known audio gaps: no pedal noise, no string resonance, no unison or soft-release shaping, no timbre filtering, no layer behaviour. All panel controls in the piano, effects, organ, synth and program sections are decorative in Phase 1.

audio.strategy: Phase 2 has three recorded, bundled, offline sample sets (Grand, Upright, Electric) played through per-note sample voices, plus three honestly synthesized types (Clav, Digital, Misc) and the Phase 1 live-synthesis voice as a labelled fallback. Every sound reaches one AudioContext through per-layer buses, the ordered effect units, the shared Rotary, a master gain, and a limiter. Recorded audio is never generated, and generated audio is never described as a recording.

generatedSources.name: Phase 1 additive piano voice (live synthesis)
generatedSources.description: Six sine partials per note with a small inharmonic stretch, velocity-dependent partial levels and low-pass cutoff, and exponential decay. Generated at note-on. Used as the labelled fallback for Grand, Upright, and Electric while their sets load or after they fail. Not a recording.

generatedSources.name: Clav (synthesized)
generatedSources.description: Sawtooth plus square oscillators through a decaying low-pass filter with a short decay and quick release. An approximation of clavinet character, not a model of the Clavinet D6 pickups (manual p. 24).

generatedSources.name: Digital (synthesized FM)
generatedSources.description: Two-operator FM: a sine carrier with a sine modulator whose index decays after the strike, giving a bell-like upper spectrum. A stand-in for digital piano character.

generatedSources.name: Marimba (synthesized)
generatedSources.description: Three inharmonic sine modes at ratios 1, 4, and 10 with fast decay on the upper two.

generatedSources.name: Simulated sympathetic string resonance
generatedSources.description: When a note is struck with String Res on and other keys are held, each held note rings at its fundamental at a low level for about 3 seconds. A simulation of the effect described on manual p. 25; no pedal-down samples are used.

generatedSources.name: Generated reverb impulse responses
generatedSources.description: Six room impulse responses generated at run time from a fixed-seed noise generator with per-type decay (Booth 0.22 s to Cathedral 4.5 s), early reflections, and spring echoes for Spring. Not recordings of real rooms.

notes: Sample files live in public/samples/ and are fetched relative to the page, so the build works offline from any folder (base './'). Nothing is fetched from the network at runtime.
The sample sets were built by tools/samples/build_piano_samples.py from the three upstream archives. The script is the provenance record for every file.
Unison, Dyn Comp, KB Touch, Timbre, Soft Release, and Master Level act on the rendered signal through gains, curves, and filters; they are not separate recordings.
Organ, Synth, and Program sound engines are not in Phase 2; their panel controls are decorative and say so.

Declared gaps: Upright has 10 soft-only roots; Grand is truncated at 10 seconds; Upright plays its full length; Electric is non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) and is shifted by up to about 4 semitones at its extremes; no pedal-down string samples and no pedal noise; soft and sostenuto pedals are not implemented (SUSTPED is); Clav and Misc timbre steps reuse the acoustic set as an approximation; the piano model dial is decorative because each type has one model.

audio.strategy: Phase 3 completes the instrument on one AudioContext. The three recorded, bundled, offline piano sample sets (Grand, Upright, Electric) are unchanged from Phase 2. Every other sound is live synthesis, declared in generatedSources: the organ (four models built from sine partials, percussion, key click, vibrato and chorus), the synth (fourteen required waveforms, filters, envelopes, LFO, voice modes), and the Phase 2 piano synthesis and fallback. Generated buffers (the synth white-noise loop, the organ key-click burst, and the reverb impulses) are generated at run time and are never described as recordings. Every sound reaches the Phase 2 graph: organ and synth chains with their own six-unit effect chains, the shared Rotary, master gain, and limiter.

generatedSources.name: Organ tone engines (B3, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1, Pipe 2)
generatedSources.description: Sine partials per drawbar, one rule per model: B3 linear per drawbar on 9 footages; Vox flat over 7 partials with the ninth drawbar dulling the upper partials; Farf on/off registers with odd-weighted partials; Pipe 1 a 1/ratio rank series; Pipe 2 the Pipe 1 engine with a brighter 1/ratio^0.7 slope (reuses the Pipe 1 engine, as the spec allows). Generated at note-on. Not recordings.

generatedSources.name: B3 percussion (2nd or 3rd harmonic, single-triggered)
generatedSources.description: One sine partial at the second or third harmonic with a linear decay of 0.25 s (fast) or 0.9 s (slow), level by soft/normal and the volume knob. Retriggers only when the layer is silent (manual p. 20).

generatedSources.name: Key click (generated noise burst)
generatedSources.description: A 6 ms burst of deterministic noise (fixed-seed generator) at note-on, at a fixed low level. Generated, not a recording.

generatedSources.name: Vibrato and chorus (LFO detune)
generatedSources.description: A 6.1 Hz sine LFO drives the detune of every partial (V1 to V3, 10 to 35 cents at full depth). C1 to C3 mix a pitch-modulated copy of the partials with the dry set at 25 to 65 percent.

generatedSources.name: Synth source recipes (Pure, Sync, Multi, Super, FM-H)
generatedSources.description: Pure: sine, triangle, saw, and square oscillators, and pulse waves from Fourier coefficients (33 percent and 10 percent duty). Multi and Super: stacks of detuned saws or squares, spread by Osc Ctrl. Sync: a second oscillator at a relative pitch of 1 to 4 times, a documented approximation of hard sync (no oscillator reset). FM 2-op: a sine carrier with a 2x modulator whose depth is Osc Ctrl.

generatedSources.name: White noise (generated loop)
generatedSources.description: A two-second loop of deterministic white noise, generated once per context. Not a recording.

generatedSources.name: Synth filters, envelopes, and LFO
generatedSources.description: LP12, LP24 (two cascaded low-pass stages), HP, and BP biquad filters with keyboard tracking, resonance, and a soft-clip drive stage. Amplifier, filter, and oscillator envelopes built from scheduled ramps; a finite decay settles at 0.7 (amplifier) or 0.5 (filter and oscillator) of its peak, and a maximum decay holds at the peak. LFO: triangle, two saws, square, and a Sample and Hold shape, which is a fixed pseudo-random periodic wave (deterministic, not a stepped random sample).

generatedSources.name: Arpeggiator sequencer (note events, no audio source)
generatedSources.description: A deterministic sequencer that schedules note-on and note-off events on a fixed step grid from the clock. It has no audio of its own; its notes are played by the synth layers.

notes: Sample files live in public/samples/ and are fetched relative to the page, so the build works offline from any folder (base './'). Nothing is fetched from the network at runtime.
The sample sets were built by tools/samples/build_piano_samples.py from the three upstream archives. The script is the provenance record for every file.
Unison, Dyn Comp, KB Touch, Timbre, Soft Release, and Master Level act on the rendered signal through gains, curves, and filters; they are not separate recordings.

Organ, synth, and program state are serializable: a program carries every supported setting, split, scene, morph, clock value, and transpose. Master Level, the performance inputs, and the bank's own selection are not saved in a program.

Declared gaps (Phase 3). Organ: B3 Bass is not offered (optional, and the panel has no switch for it); the vibrato and chorus on switch is shared by both layers, not per layer; the Vox mix drawbar is an approximation (it dulls partials at ratio 4 and up); the swell pedal, rotary stop mode, and the preset and drawbar-live modes are excluded by the spec. Synth: Samples mode, LP M, LP+HP, Sub Osc, Shape, Misc, Wave, FM inharmonic, Sound Init, the pattern editor, zig-zag, accent, pan, and KB Hold are not implemented (optional or excluded). Hard sync is approximated by a detuned pair; the Sample and Hold LFO is a fixed periodic wave; the LFO Osc Ctrl destination scales the stack's detune; Vibrato in Wheel mode reads the wheel at note-on. Arpeggiator gate length is fixed at half a step, and the Gate mode does not repurpose the range knob. Mod 1 syncs to the clock for A-Pan and Tremolo only; the other Mod 1 types are unsynced. Rotary speed is a continuous control (Slow at 0, Fast at 1), so it can be morphed. Sustain follows the piano's SUSTPED switch for all engines (no per-section SUSTPED). Store: while STORE is armed, the program buttons choose the destination without auditioning it, so the edits being stored are kept. Program: banks beyond one, Organize, categories, sorting, Solo, Prog View, and single-level undo are not implemented. Aftertouch is excluded: the A.T. morph source is decorative. The piano model dial stays decorative (one model per type).
